items.note: A politeness step up from いい (ii, "Nice, good") from Lesson 9. You hear it in ちょっと よろしいですか (chotto yoroshii desu ka), used to a busy superior.

items.english: May I have a moment of your time?

items.note: Use it to approach someone of higher status who is busy. It is more formal than the casual ちょっと (chotto) "Well, it's a bit..." from Lesson 16, which here means "a moment", not a polite refusal.

items.note: Regular 1, and the one cell the book stars as an exception. き (ki) normally gives いて (ite), as in かいて (kaite), yet いきます (ikimasu) becomes いって (itte). It is NOT an Irregular verb — only きます (kimasu) and します (shimasu) are. Don't confuse it with いて (ite), the て-form of います (imasu).

items.reviewNote: Only て-form given in text (exercise I example). The main て-form chart is an image I could not read; other て-forms may need adding from it. | Resolved at gate 1: the chart (Page_173_Image_0001) WAS read by the image specialist, and all 19 て-form cells were audited cell-by-cell against the cards — none missing.
items.note: Regular 2. Simpler than Regular 1: just change ます (masu) to て (te). みて (mite), いて (ite), おしえて (oshiete) and みせて (misete) all work this way.
Regular 1. For these the sound before ます (masu) decides the ending: い (i) → って (tte). あいます (aimasu) → あって (atte) works the same way.
